pageCache.pageTitle: Home - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Home
A small school. A world of opportunities. A place to flourish.
Set in beautiful surroundings overlooking the historic Chepstow Castle and the River Wye, Dean Close St John’s provides exceptional co-educational schooling for children aged 3 to 13. Renowned for our family-feel environment, we take pride in delivering outstanding academic and pastoral care. With flexible wraparound services, a daily bus service, and options for part-time and full-time boarding, we support the diverse needs of families.
Childhood at St John’s is about more than education — it’s about freedom, discovery, and joy. It’s a chance to climb trees, get muddy knees, light fires, take risks, and embrace challenges. It’s about laughing with friends and building bonds that last a lifetime. By fostering independence and encouraging exploration both inside and outside the classroom, we create an environment where learning becomes an exciting adventure.
Find out what makes us distinctly different
A proud member of the Dean Close Foundation since 2015, St John’s benefits from shared strength, stability and focus, enabling our staff to deliver the very best education and help every pupil flourish.

pageCache.pageTitle: Faith - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Faith
Our Christian values underpin all that we do as a school. We believe that building a strong foundation based on Love, Courage and Contribution gives the children the chance to grow long-lasting and positive friendships that are created on shared values. We welcome children and families from all faiths or secular backgrounds, and hope that our inclusive approach ensures questions relating to religion and spirituality can be shared openly.
We have a church service for the prep school once every half term, with the Foundation Chaplain coming down regularly to lead assemblies. We also mark occasions such as Remembrance Day and we hold a whole school Carol service and Christingle service to celebrate Christmas. Awe and wonder should be at the heart of learning and by encouraging children to explore our world to the full, we firmly believe that must include questions around faith.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Aims & Values - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Our Aims & Values
Our Aims
At Dean Close St John’s, we aim to nurture every pupil so that they flourish, achieving their full potential in a safe, inclusive, and values-led environment, guided by our Christian ethos. We promote academic excellence, personal growth, and respect for others, encouraging pupils to act with courage, integrity, and compassion within our school and the wider community.
Love, Contribution, Courage, Flourishing
LOVE
We encourage everyone within the Foundation to love each other with integrity, openness and abundance and we embrace vulnerability to enable depth in our love for others. We acknowledge that we have a wider responsibility to one another to be the best version of ourselves, through rest and reflection, in order to fully show love in this way. Our mission is that all people within our community will feel valued, respected and loved.
We know that each person has something valuable to offer. With a sense of humility, we aim to contribute greatly to each other and more widely beyond our immediate community.
Everyone can show courage no matter how strong or weak they may feel. Our aim is ensure that each person knows they are accepted for who they are, and in turn will be guided to show courage to try new things, take risks and impact positive change.
Our desire is that our staff and pupils lead a full and fulfilled life, in which we flourish and reach our potential. Flourishing is the aim that anchors the values of love, courage and contribution. We deeply care about quality in our teaching, high standards, inclusion and the desire not to leave anyone behind. By sincerely loving others, enabling people to feel confident to be courageous and encouraging wider contribution beyond oneself, we believe every member of our community has the ability to flourish
"Flourishing is the aim that anchors the values of love, courage and contribution."

pageCache.pageTitle: About us - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
About us
Dean Close St John's - Distinctly Different
Set in beautiful surroundings overlooking the historic Chepstow Castle, Dean Close St John’s provides exceptional co-educational schooling for children aged 3 to 13. Renowned for our family-feel environment, we take pride in delivering outstanding academic and pastoral care. With flexible wraparound services, a daily bus service, and options for part-time and full-time boarding, we support the diverse needs of families.
Childhood at Dean Close St John's School
Childhood at St John’s is about more than education — it’s about freedom, discovery, and joy. It’s a chance to climb trees, get muddy knees, light fires, take risks, and embrace challenges. It’s about laughing with friends and building bonds that last a lifetime. We understand the transformative power of the outdoors — it grounds us, inspires us, and fuels our joy. By fostering independence and encouraging exploration both inside and outside the classroom, we create an environment where learning becomes an exciting adventure.
We believe childhood is a precious time of growth, where mistakes are embraced, resilience is built, and curiosity flourishes. Supported by exceptional pastoral care and the freedom to learn in diverse settings, our pupils grow into kind, confident, and well-rounded individuals.
At St John’s, the journey matters just as much as the destination. By giving children the time and space to cherish these fleeting moments, we ensure they grow with purpose, happiness, and a lifelong love for learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal Growth - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Personal Growth
As children move into Year 7, they are all at different stages of their academic, social and emotional development. What feels like the right next step at the end of Year 6 is not always the best fit by the age of 13. This is why the Senior Prep years are such an important stage in a child's educational journey.
We understand that every child matures at their own pace, particularly during the significant years of early adolescence. Our Senior Prep environment provides the time, space and outstanding pastoral support pupils need to grow in confidence, independence and self-belief, while continuing to enjoy the benefits of an extended childhood.
Rather than being hurried towards public examinations, pupils benefit from an approach that focuses on their individual development during these formative years. With small class sizes, specialist teaching and exceptional pastoral care, we ensure that every child feels known, supported and encouraged to flourish academically, socially and emotionally.
By the end of Year 8, pupils leave us as confident, resilient and well-rounded young people, fully prepared for the opportunities and challenges of Senior School.
Ready for the Next Stage
Our preparation for Senior School is second to none, and the feedback we receive from senior school leaders is a testament to the dedication of our staff and the quality of the Senior Prep experience. Time and again, schools comment not only on our pupils’ academic readiness, but also on their confidence, character, kindness and compassion towards others.
By the end of Year 8, our pupils are well-rounded young people who are ready to embrace the opportunities and challenges of Senior School. Equipped with strong values, leadership skills and a genuine sense of purpose, they leave Dean Close St John’s prepared not just to succeed, but to make a positive difference wherever life takes them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care
At Dean Close St John’s, we believe that children flourish when they feel safe, seen and supported. Pastoral care is at the heart of everything we do, and this year we have continued to build on that foundation through our whole-school approach: the Pastoral Pathway.
The Pastoral Pathway is designed to ensure every child receives the emotional, social and mental health support they need to grow into confident, resilient and happy young people. Grounded in our core value of flourishing, it offers three tiers of care: Universal, Targeted, and Specialist.
Universal Support – For All Pupils We start with a strong foundation of universal support that every child benefits from. This includes PSHE and wellbeing lessons, daily check-ins, and our school-wide use of the Zones of Regulation to help children name and manage their emotions.
By encouraging emotional literacy, promoting self-awareness, and maintaining consistent routines, we help children understand themselves and one another better. This culture of care supports healthy friendships, builds empathy, and fosters a sense of belonging across the school.
Targeted Support – For Some Pupils Some children need a little extra support to navigate life’s ups and downs, and we’re here to walk alongside them. Through small-group ELSA interventions, TEAA (Time to Express, Acknowledge and Act) sessions, and social skills groups, we create safe, nurturing spaces for pupils to explore their feelings and build confidence.
These sessions give children the tools to express themselves, develop their voice, and strengthen positive peer relationships in a supportive environment.
Specialist Support – For Individual Needs For pupils who may be facing more complex emotional or mental health challenges, we offer more specialised care. This might include 1:1 ELSA sessions, counselling or psychotherapy with one of our trainee therapists, or collaboration with external professionals.
This tier ensures that children with individual needs are met with compassion, expertise and a personalised approach. Every child’s story matters, and we work closely with families to provide the right support at the right time.
A Culture of Compassion and Connection What makes the Pastoral Pathway so powerful is the way it permeates the whole school culture. It’s not just about formal interventions — it’s about the small, daily moments of kindness and connection. Whether it’s a teacher noticing a child who’s feeling anxious, a quiet check-in during break time, or celebrating the progress a child has made in expressing their emotions — it all matters.
At St John’s, pastoral care isn’t an add-on. It’s who we are. And we will continue to grow our commitment to supporting every child to flourish, both in and beyond the classroom.
If you ever have questions, concerns, or feel your child may benefit from additional support, please don’t hesitate to get in touch. Our doors are always open, and we are here to help.
Lisa Duncan Designated Safeguarding and Pastoral Lead
To learn more how we create a positive, inclusive, and respectful environment at St John's please visit our Health & Wellbeing page.

pageCache.pageTitle: Holiday Club - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Holiday Club
At St John's, we offer two exciting holiday clubs during half-term breaks and school holidays, providing reliable support for families outside term time.
Mini Lions Holiday Club
Our Mini Lions Holiday Club is run by St John's staff and is specially designed for children aged 3 to 7 years.
Open to children from all schools, Mini Lions offers a range of creative, sporting, nature-based, and arts and crafts activities in a safe and nurturing setting, helping children learn, play and make new friends during the holidays.
P.L.A.Y Active Holiday Club
The P.L.A.Y Active Holiday Club is delivered by our trusted external partner, P.L.A.Y Active, and is available for children aged 5 to 12 years. The club typically runs throughout the school holidays and also offers holiday club provision on INSET days. A limited number of places may be available for younger children.
Open to children from all schools, the club offers a wide variety of energetic and fun-filled activities, including sports, games, crafts and outdoor adventures, designed to keep children active, engaged and entertained throughout the holidays.
Please contact P.L.A.Y Active directly at playactive19@gmail.com for further information.
Autumn Half Term Dates: Monday 26th October - Thursday 29th October 2026
Christmas holiday dates are coming soon!
All St John's Parents with children in Pre Prep will have received an email invite to book on to the camp. If you have not received an email, please click here and let us know.
External Parents, please click here to register.
Our Pre-Prep Holiday Club is a warm, nurturing space where young children can have fun, stay active, and keep learning during the holidays.
Run by our own experienced Dean Close St John’s staff, each day is filled with exciting activities like sport, nature exploration, or art – all designed to support your child’s growth and happiness.
With a focus on care, confidence, and creativity – and the values of the Dean Close Foundation at its heart – our Holiday Club ensures every child has fun, feels safe, and is fully supported throughout the day.
P.L.A.Y Active holiday camp will also run on the INSET Day on Friday 23 October, providing childcare and activities throughout the day.
Please contact P.L.A.Y Active directly at playactive19@gmail.com for further information.

pageCache.pageTitle: Little Trees Tutshill - Dean Close Little Trees Nurseries
pageCache.text:
Little Trees Tutshill
Little Trees Day Nursery Tutshill (on the site of Dean Close St John's school) provides a nurturing environment where children aged three months to four years old can learn and grow together. We are passionate about giving your child the very best experiences to ensure they develop into well rounded little individuals.
Sara Guerreiro - Nursery Manager
We are delighted to welcome Sara as the Nursery Manager at Little Trees Tutshill. She has been passionate about working with children since the age of 15 and holds a degree in Childhood Studies. Sara brings a strong commitment to child development and high-quality early years education.
With over five years’ experience working within the NHS, Sara has developed a thorough understanding of children’s wellbeing and the importance of working in close partnership with families. This experience shapes her nurturing and inclusive approach, ensuring every child feels safe, supported, and valued.
Sara believes children learn best when they feel secure and inspired. She is dedicated to creating an environment that encourages curiosity, independence, and confidence, allowing each child to flourish and reach their full potential.
Outside of work, Sara enjoys spending time outdoors, listening to music, and going on adventures with family and friends. She brings this enthusiasm for exploration into the nursery, embracing every day as an opportunity to learn and grow alongside the children.
To support her, she has a highly qualified and experienced team. Her staff are dedicated to giving young children the care and attention they need to aid their social, emotional and intellectual development.
Our nursery workers are up to Level 5 qualified in Childcare and Education or are working towards or beyond this qualification. We offer training and continued professional development to all employees.
We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. All our employees undergo child protection screening, including checks with past employers and the Disclosure and Barring Service. Every member of staff is trained in paediatric first aid and child protection, giving you added peace of mind.
Little Trees Day Nursery Tutshill is open 7:30am to 6:00pm Monday – Friday (with the exception of bank holidays).

pageCache.pageTitle: Kindergarten - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Kindergarten
Kindergarten offers a wonderful introduction to school life within a secure and stimulating environment specifically designed for young children. Our aim is to help each child become school-ready, progressing to Reception and beyond as confident, happy learners.
With an excellent pupil-to-teacher ratio—an average of 12 pupils per class—our dedicated Kindergarten teacher and classroom assistant provide tailored learning support, ensuring every child’s individual needs are met.
A Balanced and Enriching Curriculum The Kindergarten curriculum is thoughtfully structured to balance learning with fun and closely follows the Creative Early Years Curriculum. Children benefit from specialist teaching in Drama, Music, and PE, fostering their skills and creativity from an early age.
Enriched Learning Experiences Classroom activities are enhanced by regular visits to our on-site Forest School, offering exciting opportunities for outdoor exploration and discovery. Additionally, children have the chance to shine in various performance opportunities, including our much-anticipated Christmas and Summer productions.
Outstanding Facilities and Services
The Kindergarten at Dean Close St John’s benefits from a range of excellent facilities and services designed to enhance your child’s school experience, including:

pageCache.pageTitle: Years 1 & 2 - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Years 1 & 2
A Broad, Balanced, and Vibrant Curriculum
Our curriculum ignites a love of learning through engaging, topic-based teaching methods that captivate and inspire children. By exploring a diverse range of topics, pupils develop their literacy and numeracy skills alongside weekly lessons in French, swimming, PE, Games, and Music. We follow the basic framework of the Key Stage One National Curriculum as a guideline, ensuring comprehensive development across all areas of learning.
Personalized Learning for Every Child We employ a combination of group and individual work to cater to children with varying levels of attainment and ability. Each child’s unique strengths are nurtured and encouraged, helping them reach their full potential. A high teacher-to-pupil ratio allows us to provide tailored support, enabling every child to learn and grow at their own pace. Progress is celebrated with immediate positive praise and rewards, fostering confidence and a sense of achievement.
Specialist Teaching and Outdoor Learning Dedicated specialist teachers from the Prep School deliver lessons in French, Music, and Physical Education, giving children an early advantage in developing these skills. Classrooms feature integral outdoor areas, offering an additional dimension to learning. The nature garden, forest school, and adventure playground further enhance outdoor exploration and activity, enriching the children’s experiences.
Enriched Learning Opportunities Trips and visits are an integral part of our academic curriculum, supporting and extending classroom learning. We also invite a variety of visitors, such as “Florence Nightingale,” Braces Bread, Pirate Pete, and Roaming Reptiles, to share their expertise and passion, bringing topics to life in exciting and interactive ways.
A Welcoming Open-Door Policy We operate an open-door policy, providing parents with the opportunity to discuss the day’s activities or any questions directly with staff. In addition, we regularly host open classroom events, where parents are invited to join us. These occasions allow children to proudly share their achievements, fostering a strong connection between school and home.
A Caring and Stimulating Environment Our dedicated staff create a safe, nurturing, and stimulating environment where children can grow, develop, and flourish at their own pace and stage of development.
Seamless Transition to Prep School With regular visits to the Prep School—such as enjoying lunches, using the Main Hall, and accessing the computer room—combined with teachers who know each child individually, the transition to the Prep School is seamless and comfortable.

pageCache.pageTitle: Growing Leaders - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Growing Leaders
Our Values
At Dean Close St John’s, our values of Love, Courage and Contribution are at the heart of school life. As pupils move into the Senior Prep years, they are encouraged to take on greater responsibility and leadership, living out these values in their daily actions. As the oldest pupils in the school, they are expected to lead by example, serving as positive role models within our community.
Knowing Yourself
As pupils enter their teenage years, we gently encourage them to develop a deeper understanding of themselves. Through guided reflection and discussion, they explore their individual strengths, areas for growth, interests and talents, helping them to build confidence, self-awareness and resilience. This unique approach enables us to support each child as an individual, ensuring they can thrive both in and beyond the classroom.
Leadership and Responsibility
Leadership is an important part of life at Dean Close St John’s, and pupils are encouraged to take on increasing levels of responsibility as they progress through the School. During the Senior Prep years, there is a greater emphasis on character development, helping pupils to understand the qualities of effective leadership and the importance of leading with integrity, kindness and confidence.
Pupils are given meaningful opportunities to shape school life, contribute to decision-making and make a positive difference within the community. Leadership roles include Head of School, House Captains, Heads of Sport, Music and Boarding, as well as a range of other positions that enable pupils to develop responsibility, teamwork and initiative.
Through these experiences, pupils build the confidence, communication skills and sense of responsibility that will serve them well in Senior School and beyond.
Pupil Ambassadors
Taking on responsibility is a vital part of life at Dean Close St John’s. Pupils have many opportunities to represent the School, from welcoming visitors and leading tours to performing at events and supporting the wider community. These experiences build confidence, communication skills and a sense of service, helping pupils become positive role models who lead by example and make a meaningful contribution.

pageCache.pageTitle: Visits and Open Days  - Dean Close St John's School
pageCache.text:
Visits and Open Days
It is our pleasure to welcome you to Dean Close St John’s, whether you join us for an Open Morning, a personal visit, or explore our school online.
Choosing the right school is an important decision, and we believe that nothing compares to experiencing the feel of a place in person. We are proud of our warm, family-feel school, where every child is known, valued and encouraged to reach their full potential. During your visit to St John’s, you will meet our Head, teachers and pupils, see learning in action, and gain a genuine insight into everyday life at our school.
We look forward to welcoming you and your family, showing you around our excellent facilities, and giving you a real sense of what makes Dean Close St John’s such a special place for children to learn, grow and flourish.
Upcoming Open Morning dates for 2026-27 academic year:
Friday, 2nd October 2026
Friday, 13th November 2026
Our Open Morning events are the perfect opportunity to discover Dean Close St John’s, whether you are looking for a place for your child in our Kindergarten (ages 3+), Pre-Prep (Reception to Year 2), Prep (Years 3 to 6) or Senior Prep (Years 7 and 8).
We plan to conclude the Open Morning at 11:00am, but if you have any further questions or would like to stay a little longer, you are very welcome to do so.
After the Open Morning, there is an option to book an individual meeting or a 'Discover & Flourish Session' with one of our Heads of Department (please see more details below). These will normally take place from 11.00am onwards. We will confirm all arrangements and timings with you prior to your visit.
Children are very welcome to attend this initial visit, or you may prefer to visit first and bring them along at a later date, whichever feels right for your family.
If you missed one of our Open Mornings but would still like to visit, we’d be delighted to welcome you for a personal tour. Please contact us at admissions@deanclosestjohns.org.uk to arrange a time that suits you.
Is your child particularly interested in Science, Mathematics, Art, Drama, Music, Languages, Sport, or another area?
We would be delighted to tailor your visit and arrange an opportunity for you to meet the relevant Head of Department. This will allow you to learn more about the opportunities available and ask any specific questions you may have.
If your child would enjoy it, we would also be happy to arrange a Discover & Flourish Session to help them become fully involved in the visit through a hands-on experience. This might include trying musical instruments, taking part in a sports coaching session or art workshop, exploring a science activity, or discovering another area of particular interest.
If you would like to arrange a personal meeting or Discover & Flourish Session, please let us know when booking your Open Morning or personal visit using the form below, or simply email admissions@deanclosestjohns.org.uk before your visit. Our Head of Admissions will then be in touch to discuss the arrangements and help tailor your experience to your child's individual strengths, interests and aspirations.

We plan to conclude the Open Morning at 11:00am, but if you have any further questions or would like to stay a little longer, you are very welcome to do so.
After the Open Morning, there is an option to book an individual meeting or a 'Discover & Flourish Session' with one of our Heads of Department (please see more details below). Children are very welcome to attend this initial visit, or you may prefer to visit first and bring them along at a later date, whichever feels right for your family.
If you missed one of our Open Mornings but would still like to visit, we’d be delighted to welcome you for a personal tour. Please contact us at admissions@deanclosestjohns.org.uk to arrange a time that suits you.
Is your child particularly interested in Science, Mathematics, Art, Drama, Music, Languages, Sport, or another area?

This might include trying musical instruments, taking part in a sports coaching session or art workshop, exploring a science activity, or discovering another area of particular interest.
If you would like to arrange a personal meeting or Discover & Flourish Session, please let us know when booking your Open Morning or personal visit using the form below, or simply email admissions@deanclosestjohns.org.uk before your visit. pageCache.text:
Music
At St John's, we feel that music is a vital part of our curriculum, supported through extra-curricular clubs and 1:1 lessons with our team of visiting music teachers. Research shows that musical education is essential to a child's cognitive development, offering a creative outlet that encourages students to cooperate with others and to explore their own musical individuality.
From their earliest years in Kindergarten to our flourishing Year 8s, every year group receives weekly class music lessons with our music teachers. Our varied music curriculum offers our children opportunities to compose, perform and interpret a wide variety of music from around the world. Whole class instrumental lessons take place from Key Stage 1 upwards on a whole host of instruments from the pBuzz to the violin, and our Year 7s and 8s explore their music technology skills in their composition lessons.
Visiting Music Teachers
We have a team of highly skilled visiting music teachers who share their wealth of knowledge with our children, including performers from the West End and world class brass band champions.
Instruments offered include:
Strings - violin, cello
Guitar - classical and rock
Brass - trumpet, trombone, euphonium, French horn
Singing - classical and music theatre
Woodwind - recorder, clarinet, saxophone and flute
Our extra-curricular music clubs include the school orchestra, rock band, Beginner Strings Club, String Ensemble, Beginner Brass, and Wind/Brass Ensemble.
Choirs
St John's has a strong history of choral singing and our choirs regularly lead our school events, concerts and church services. Our three choirs are:
Little Voices - Years 1 and 2
Junior Choir - Years 3 - 5
Senior Choir - Years 6 – 8
